summary: No repository table pairs mating system with male weapon size across a broad animal sample: PanTHERIA and AVONET (the assessor-named tables) lack both variables, while three Dryad datasets cover pieces for birds (spurs), bovids (horns plus monogamy/polygyny) and fiddler crabs (claws plus mating system); the Lukas and Clutton-Brock mammal compilation named by an assessor was not found as a dataset.
next_step: Compile a mammal (or bovid+cervid) table from the bovid Dryad dataset plus a published mating-system source, and pre-register the phylogenetic regression with body size as covariate.
obstacles_confirmed: Combat intensity and 'special weapons' require subjective coding.
Mating system and weapon inventories are spread through handbooks and supplements rather than one global table.
Birds are less consistently coded than large mammals.
